HARD-GATE at line 256 covers inline-fix + parallel-bypass axes but omits pre-commitment-to-scope-reduction. Live incident confirmed the gap; no further probe needed.

Concrete edit (file: plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md):

Block prohibits batch-entry pre-commitment with three observed surface phrasings enumerated verbatim ('I'll commit per fix and stop if context tightens', 'top 3-4 actionable then stop', 'time to be disciplined'). Affirms: 'Process EVERY ticket. Batch size N is not a shutdown signal; it is the work.' Cross-refs Phase H Step 13 / f9b5-213b for the only valid shutdown path.

2. EXTEND f9b5-213b enumeration at lines 788-793 with one new bullet citing d260-f307 and the verbatim phrasings, so the same drift axis is recognized in both the entry guard and the between-batch guard.

KERNEL: minimal-fix — co-locates one new constraint axis at the decision site (Kernel principle); narrow scope (does not touch existing inline-fix/parallel-bypass guards); explicit constraints (verbatim surface phrasings, not paraphrased); verifiable (re-verify by re-reading section with N tickets visible — prohibition now in local context).
